manifest.title: Firefox Sync Server
manifest.author: Mozilla Services
manifest.description:
Mozilla's Sync Storage server (syncstorage-rs) lets you store your Firefox Sync data on your own server. Bookmarks, history, passwords, open tabs, add-ons and preferences are encrypted in the browser before they are uploaded, so the server never sees them in plain text.

Sign-in still uses your Mozilla account. Only the storage of the encrypted sync data moves to your Cloudron.

### Features

* Sync for Firefox desktop and Firefox for Android
* Includes the Tokenserver that hands out storage credentials after Mozilla account sign-in
* Data is stored in PostgreSQL and included in Cloudron backups
* Option to block new accounts once your own devices are connected
manifest.changelog:
* Initial version with syncstorage-rs 0.24.1
* Syncstorage and Tokenserver backed by the Cloudron PostgreSQL addon
* Daily purge of expired records
manifest.postInstallMessage:
This app has no web interface. Point Firefox at it **before** signing in to your Mozilla account:

* **Desktop**: open `about:config`, set `identity.sync.tokenserver.uri` to `$CLOUDRON-APP-ORIGIN/1.0/sync/1.5` and restart Firefox.
* **Android**: open **Settings → About Firefox**, tap the logo five times, go back to **Settings → Sync Debug** and set **Custom Sync server** to `$CLOUDRON-APP-ORIGIN/1.0/sync/1.5`.

If you are already signed in, sign out, change the setting and sign in again.

Anyone with a Mozilla account who knows this URL can store data here. After your devices are connected, set `SYNC_TOKENSERVER__ALLOW_NEW_USERS=false` in `/app/data/env.sh` with the File Manager and restart the app.
